subject.title: [BUG] exec tool: aborted run wedges subsequent exec calls in same session (regression from PR #94412)

question: Should #102006 be tracked as covered by the #102160 run-lifecycle stack after merge/live validation, or should maintainers require a separate focused exec-after-abort fix and reproduction?
rationale: The issue is a concrete production bug, but the best owner boundary may be the broader run-lifecycle state-machine work rather than another narrow exec-specific patch.

options.title: Keep open for lifecycle validation
options.body: Track #102006 against #102160 and close only after merged proof shows a later foreground `exec` works in the same session after abort.

options.title: Require a focused exec fix
options.body: Ask for a small targeted patch and real repro if the lifecycle stack does not directly cover the `exec` managed-process cleanup path.

options.title: Fold into the umbrella only
options.body: Move discussion to #101863 and close this issue as covered by the design thread, accepting less precise validation for the reported symptom.

recommendation.title: Keep open for lifecycle validation
recommendation.body: Track #102006 against #102160 and close only after merged proof shows a later foreground `exec` works in the same session after abort.

likelyOwner.reason: The open lifecycle design and integration PR are the most likely current decision point for whether this symptom is fixed centrally or needs a focused follow-up.
